title: Runtime feedback fragmentarium — sprint notes & low-effort probes
content:
Summary:

This note collects short customer vignettes we heard in the last three sprints, a prioritized list of low-effort probes to reduce pain, and a set of hypotheses for engineering follow-ups. Goal: capture the signal quickly, ship small mitigations that improve customer experience within 1–3 sprints, and surface a small set of medium-term product changes for roadmap planning.

Tone: rough, patchwork, prioritized by expected impact/effort. Lots of open questions and suggested owners. Treat as a working scratchpad.

Top customer vignettes (condensed):

1) Batch / batching surprises (mid-market analytics app)
- Symptom: customers running mixed-length inference jobs see a wide latency tail when a small number of long prompts are introduced into a steady stream of short prompts.
- Customer impact: timeouts in product pipelines; engineering teams hammer retries which increases cost.
- Anecdote: "Works fine for 90% of requests, but a 5% long-prompt spike spikes latency to 10-20x for those sessions." (NPS call, 2027-11-02).

2) KV-cache invalidation friction (enterprise assistant for docs)
- Symptom: cache priming works but cache misses occur after small prompt edits; customers don't have an intuitive knob to control when to flush or reuse embeddings/KV prefixes.
- Customer impact: unpredictable token cost and quality regressions during editing workflows.

3) Routing fallback opacity (SaaS multi-tenant integration)
- Symptom: auto-fallback to lower-cost model variants triggers silently during capacity pressure. The app sees subtle degradation in response style/length.
- Customer impact: support tickets, blame routed to model quality rather than routing policy.

Measured signals we can use (existing telemetry pointers):
- 95th/99th percentile latency by route and by sequence-length bucket (console metric: route.latency.p99.seq-buckets).
- KV-cache hit rate by customer and by route (derived metric: kv.hit-rate).
- Model-variant-fallback count by time interval (routing.fallback.counter).
- Token billing delta vs baseline (billing.delta.per-route).

Hypotheses (short):
- H1: Mixed-length batching algorithms are optimizing throughput but not respecting latency SLOs for tail-heavy workloads.
- H2: Customers lack pragmatic controls for KV cache lifetime, prefixes, and explicit flush semantics; default heuristics are too aggressive for editing workflows.
- H3: Fallbacks lack transparent signalling to customers; without a visible downgrade event the UX teams chase the wrong root cause.

Low-effort probes (ranked by time-to-run / likely impact):

A) Expose a per-route "tail-protect" flag (config only) — 1 sprint spike
- What: config that disables mixing long sequences with short within the same micro-batch (effectively caps batch packing depth when long seqs present).
- Why: mitigates p99 tail without touching core batching algorithm.
- Risks: small throughput loss; needs billing telemetry check.
- Owner: Diego (spike) / Priya (telemetry).

B) Add a KV-cache "hint" header and a console toggle — 2 sprints
- What: allow clients to attach a header (kv-hint: keep|flush|session) and show a toggle in Console per-route.
- Why: gives customers a simple lever for editing-heavy flows.

- Quick UX: default = keep; admin can flip to session-flush for document editors.
- Owner: Evan (runtime) / Janelle (console).

C) Emit an explicit event when fallback used and surface in Console + webhook — 1 sprint
- What: routing emits routing.fallback.event with original and fallback model IDs; Console shows a red badge and optional webhook for ops team.
- Why: developers immediately know routing caused the quality drop.
- Owner: Samir (routing) / Product ops.

D) Canary config: early-bucket isolation for long requests — 1 sprint
- What: small change that isolates long requests into dedicated queues for a subset of customers to measure cost/latency trade-offs.
- Why: cheap experiment to measure throughput loss vs latency gain.
- Owner: Priya / SRE.

Medium-term engineering asks (worth roadmap tickets):
- Adaptive batching that takes latency SLOs and seq-length distributions as input (RW-2412).
- Fine-grained KV policy engine (session vs prefix vs explicit flush) with UI and API first-class support.
- Routing transparency improvements: annotated response headers + historical fallback timeline in Console.

Quick wins (ship in <2 sprints):
- Add fallback event emission (C).
- Add configurable per-route batch-cap that prevents mixing of sequences above threshold (A, simple config).
- Console polish: show kv-hit-rate and fallback counts on the route summary page.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many customers would accept slightly higher average latency for better p99? Need survey or in-product prompt.
- Billing model: do we bill by actual token consumption per request after we start isolating long prompts? (billing edge-case with reserved dedicated)
- How will isolates affect GPU packing efficiency for Dedicated clusters under mixed load? Need small collect experiment.

Risk & mitigation notes:
- Risk: exposing too many knobs will confuse customers. Mitigation: default-safe configs + recommended presets ("editor-friendly", "throughput-first").
- Risk: telemetry gaps. Mitigation: add metrics alongside probes and gate rollouts behind a measurement check.

Next steps (immediate):
- Run spike A (tail-protect config) this week; measure p99 and throughput delta for 10 seeded customers (owner: Diego).
- Implement fallback event emission (owner: Samir).
- Draft short in-product survey for route owners about willingness to accept avg latency increase for p99 improvements (owner: Janelle).

Notes / crumbs (raw quotes):
- "We had to double our timeout just because one sequence in the batch was huge." — Integration eng, healthcare customer, 2027-11-05.
- "I don’t know if it was a model or your service, there was no indicator." — Head of ML platform at FinApp, 2027-11-11.

Slack threads referenced:
- #runtime-feedback (pinned: thread 2027-11-03 mixed-length tails)
- #sre-ops (incident RW-2547, 2027-11-08)

Owners / proposed micro-PRs (short list):
- runtime: add "route.batch_cap" flag (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/812) — Diego
- routing: fallback-event schema + webhook (RFC -> PR) — Samir
- console: route summary widgets for kv-hit-rate + fallback count — Janelle

If you're reading this and want to propose an alternate low-effort probe, add a short note in the Confluence page linked above or drop a message in #runtime-feedback.

-- end --
